mentl/dedf269:
Six iterations since the last change to src/. inf_add_row was the last built
thing; since then a doc true-up, a retraction, a measurement, an isolation and
a stamp -- each ending "the build is next", each next iteration finding
something new to measure. Step 3's "a missing stamp means the iteration's
entire output is the stamp" is a legitimate hatch against building blind, and
I have been living in it.

Closed three ways. A stamp is a DEBT: if the previous iteration's output was a
design stamp, this one builds that design -- not a new item, not another
measurement of it, not a refinement of the stamp. Measuring is an output only
when it CHANGES what gets built; a measurement that confirms the plan is the
build's first step, not a substitute for it. And the independent-item escape,
for when a fork is Morgan's, releases the FORK and never the debt -- a
stamped, unforked design outranks any independent item.

Plus a counter: two consecutive iterations landing no change to src/ or lib/
means the third either builds or opens its report with the one sentence
naming what structurally prevents it. Docs and measurements are real work and
this loop has produced good ones, but a run of them with nothing built is the
medium standing still while the prose about it improves.

image and emits with the source absent: the frontier leg deletes main.mn
and the emission stays byte-identical to the cold run's — the projection
rode the image.

The restructure that made it sound deleted a gate instead of extending
it. Under the arm-form rehydrate, a resume verb would need the resuming
process to replicate the persisting process's install and allocation
prefix — its argv alone shifts every chain-node address — because a
dispatch bracket writes back a pre-swap world as the arm returns. That
one write was the whole reason the world fingerprint existed. rehydrate
dissolves into image_resume, a direct substrate restore with no arm and

benign tail after the last perform, and every post-swap dispatch walks
the restored $world_g. The world is image-resident end to end, an image
is resumable from any same-build process, and the fingerprint, its walk,
and its wire field are deleted rather than carried.

path, the warm path, and the resume verb all run exactly it. The wire is

Root cause found: inferred_type returned TString for ALL Concat (++) ops.
Functions returning concatenated lists got TString as their return type.
Chained ++ like [fn_def] ++ inner ++ rest dispatched the second ++ to
str_concat instead of list_concat, corrupting the list.

chain until it finds a ListExpr (→ TList) or a string literal (→ TString).
Also follows MatchExpr, IfExpr, BlockExpr, and Call to determine the
actual concat result type.

pass. Full pipe still crashes — 74 remaining val_concat sites in compiled

two-top/de8d73c:
Two crash reports reached me with nothing to read. Android release logging
went to stderr/logcat only, on the reasoning that NativeActivity gives no
stable writable cwd. logcat is a ring buffer, so the panic had rolled out
long before the phone got walked back to a desk, and an unwinding Rust panic
leaves no tombstone either.

paths::shared_dir() answers the writable-directory objection and has for a
while; the recorder has been writing tapes there all along. Release Android
now keeps stderr for live adb logcat and adds a daily-rotated file beside
the replays. A panic hook writes payload and location to crash.log in the
same directory, so the next crash survives the walk back:

  adb pull /sdcard/Android/data/<pkg>/files/crash.log

Failure to open the log directory degrades to stderr rather than panicking.
The release profile is default panic=unwind, so the hook runs.
perennials/de6ebaf:
The transform collapsed any warning containing "toxic" or "poison" into a bare
"Toxic" label and threw the rest of the sentence away. That is wrong in both
directions.

Asparagus reads "Toxic fruits" upstream and rendered as "Toxic" beside "Edible:
Shoots, Stem". Chokecherry and apricot say "Poisonous seeds" while the app lists
the seed as edible and never names the hazard. Wild garlic says "Might be
mistaken for poisonous plants", which is a warning about identification, and we
labelled the plant itself toxic; it is edible, and its real danger is that it
resembles lily-of-the-valley.

Carry the verbatim sentence through as `cautions` and show it on the plant page,
naming the edible parts next to it. The coarse labels stay, for filtering only.
Reclassify look-alike warnings as "Lookalike risk" instead of toxicity.

Also gate the refresh. replaceAll truncates before inserting, so a short pull
from an upstream outage would have destroyed the dataset and served the wreckage.
Refuse any refresh that returns under 90% of the stored count.
